description: The Maryland Department of the Environment keeps public data on bypasses, combined sewer overflows and sanitary sewer overflows that sewer system owners and operators report to it, from January 2005 to the latest update, on the state's open data portal. Incidents from January 2005 to January 2023 are in one dataset and those reported since February 2023 are in a second dataset that is updated monthly. The page notes that all public sewer owners must report but some incidents may not be, and that overflow amounts are estimated by best professional judgement or measured by flow devices where available. Coverage: one state, 2005 to the present, at the level of reported incidents. Access: free open data tables; the licence is not stated on the page read, and the columns were not inspected. Caveats: under-reporting, estimated volumes, and a change in dataset from 2023. It supports sewer overflow frequency and exposure analysis and resilience studies, and relates to the EPA NPDES overflow events and the Canadian CSO volumes already in the catalogue.
